article_title: PHP 8.6 Makes Session Cookies Secure by Default, but an Old php.ini Template Can Silently Cancel the Change
summary: Clean Analysis on PHP 8.6's session-default hardening and the php.ini-production override gap; all ~19 quotes verified verbatim against raw source text, and the only automated finding (an allowlist gap for wiki.php.net and rajekevin.fr) was resolved by independently confirming both as legitimate primary/expert sources and adding them to the allowlist — not a content defect, so no corrections record is needed.

content_preview.title: PHP 8.6 Makes Session Cookies Secure by Default, but an Old php.ini Template Can Silently Cancel the Change
content_preview.summary: PHP 8.6, released November 19, ships three session-cookie defaults hardened under a core developer's RFC. An independent developer's analysis finds the hardening only takes effect if nothing overrides it, and PHP's own packaged php.ini templates are one of the things that can.

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured Analysis (three session defaults, the php.ini-production override gap, Symfony/Laravel framework behavior, the SameSite=Lax payment-redirect trade-off, verification commands). Facts, RFC text, and Dourepoulle's independent analysis are kept clearly distinct throughout.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 4 sources read in full from decompressed .html.gz snapshots (sha256-verified against manifest; all suspicious_patterns null, no errors). Performed a literal quote-by-quote audit of every double-quoted span (~19 quotes) against the raw extracted text of all 4 pages (php.net release notes, the wiki.php.net RFC, The Register, rajekevin.fr): 'Faster, Safer, More Powerful', 'Sessions are now more secure by default...', the RFC's 'have security implications but ship with defaults that leave applications unnecessarily exposed', 'to pre-plant a known session ID and wait for a victim to authenticate against it', Sowa's 'the built-in files handler checks whether a session file for that ID exists on disk...' (quoted identically by both the RFC context and The Register, cross-confirmed), the RFC's 'Without it, a forged form or link on an attacker-controlled site can trigger authenticated requests using the victim's session', The Register's 'a swarm of unearthed vulnerabilities has plagued PHP since October...', 'responded with a coordinated release of patched versions...seven critical remote code execution (RCE) flaws in one sweep', 'blocking client-side JavaScript from reading the session ID, which could otherwise be stolen to masquerade as the user', 'For administrators, this PHP update round may be a bit of a shambles', and Dourepoulle's 'explicitly sets the old values', 'PHP 8.6's version has been aligned with the RFC', the full 'if your deployment reuses the old php.ini...' passage (independently corroborated by The Register quoting the identical sentence from the same post), 'the official php Docker image enables no php.ini until you copy one of the two templates it ships', 'forces use_strict_mode to 1 in its constructor, whatever php.ini says', 'most applications won't see a thing', 'No error shows up; the user is just logged out', and 'the CLI and PHP-FPM often read different php.ini files' — every one matched the raw source text verbatim. No fabricated or misattributed quotes found.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: No fabricated specifics. The three session-default changes (use_strict_mode, cookie_httponly, cookie_samesite), the RFC's unanimous-per-setting vote, and the php.ini-production diff between the 8.5 and 8.6 branches are all independently confirmed in the raw source text, not just taken from the writer's framing.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral; RFC text, PHP's own release notes, The Register's reporting, and Dourepoulle's independent analysis are clearly attributed and kept separate from each other throughout.
editor_notes.originality: No prior Herald coverage of PHP 8.6's session-default changes found (grep across src/content/articles/ for php 8.6 / session.use_strict_mode / session cookie surfaced only the unrelated beta/RC, license, and RCE-vulnerability articles already cross-referenced in the piece's own body).
editor_notes.allowlist_review: The automated warning flagged wiki.php.net and rajekevin.fr as not on the allowlist. wiki.php.net is the PHP project's own RFC wiki — hosting the canonical text of the RFC that shipped in PHP 8.6, a primary source. rajekevin.fr is the engineering blog of Rajekevin Dourepoulle, a backend software engineer whose post performs original, verifiable technical analysis (diffing the actual php.ini-production template files between branches, reading Symfony's source code) and is itself independently cited by The Register's own coverage — an individual credentialed-expert technical blog, consistent with how this policy has treated similar expert blogs. Both added to config/source_allowlist.txt with justification comments; not a content defect, no corrections record needed.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: A rigorously sourced, accurate Analysis meeting all format requirements (1,235 words, 4 sources, 2 independent of the PHP project by outlet — The Register and rajekevin.fr — against php.net/wiki.php.net as the vendor/primary pair), with every one of roughly 19 quotes independently verified verbatim. Featured candidacy: 2 - a well-reported, practically useful piece (the php.ini override gap is a genuine operational trap many deployments will hit on upgrade) for a broad developer audience running one of the most widely deployed server-side languages, with original cross-source corroboration, not just a release-notes rewrite.
